Brams and Kilgour (2001) generalise this concept and introduce a class of SCRs called q-approval fall-back bargaining, where q is the required quantity of support that can vary from a single voter up to unanimity. Different choices of q lead to different SCRs. Considering n voters, the choice of q = 1 corresponds to the plurality rule, q = 2 coincides with the majoritarian compromise and q = n represents a bargaining procedure called fall-back bargaining, which has been further analysed by Kibris and Sertel (2007) and Congar and Merlin (2012).
